_about: Inputs for scripts/cost_model.py. A PROPOSED plan for a future school pilot (via SFIC field-testing support); nothing here was tested in a school. Software is Rs 0 in every scenario; deployment costs are listed separately so none are hidden.

software_cost_inr.source: docs/COST_AND_LICENSES.md: every dependency is free/open source, no paid service, API key or hosting (backend runs on a school laptop).

phone_price_inr.source: Team estimate, online retail price, Oct 2026: budget Android phone.

earphone_price_inr.source: Team estimate, online retail price, Oct 2026: wired earphones with inline mic.

minutes_per_child.source: Planning input: test ~2-2.5 min from our device trials (session durations in scripts/analyze_phase4.py; CLAIMS P4/P5 rows) plus setup, a team estimate. Re-measure in team tests (docs/TEAM_TEST_PROTOCOL.md).

screening_hours_per_phone_per_day.source: Planning input, team proposal: one hour of screening per phone per school day.

students_per_phone.source: Planning guideline, team proposal: limits how long a screening round runs per phone (about 1 month at 250), not student time; each student misses about 5 minutes once a year.

school_sizes.source: Design choice: example school sizes for the cost-per-child table.

students_per_class.source: TODO(source): typical class size, used only to count class teachers in scenario C. Planning placeholder.

teacher_cost_inr_per_hour.source: TODO(source): optional. Screening may be part of existing school-health duties, so teacher time is reported in minutes; a rupee value is added only when sourced.

future_sms_cost_inr_per_message.source: TODO(source): reminders are stubbed today (logged, never sent). Real SMS is a later-round roadmap item and a future cost, shown separately.

future_sms_messages_per_referral.source: PLACEHOLDER: e.g. a camp reminder and a missed-camp reminder per referred child.

A_school_phone.label: A. School phone + earphones (recommended)
A_school_phone.notes: The school buys a phone + earphones (Rs 10,400 per kit). One calibrated phone+earphone pair gives consistent test levels; child data stays on a school device. Buy every phone of the same model with the same earphone model.

B_teacher_phone.label: B. Teacher's own phone, school buys earphones
B_teacher_phone.notes: Cheapest. Not recommended until per-model calibration exists (roadmap): each phone model needs its own calibration, test levels vary across models until then, and child data sits on a personal phone.

C_kit_per_class_teacher.label: C. One earphone kit per class teacher, on their own phones
C_kit_per_class_teacher.notes: Its advantage is speed, not cost: every class teacher screens their own class at the same time, so the whole school finishes in about the days one class takes (see the days column). It costs more than B (one kit per class instead of one per 250 students) and less than A (no phones bought). The same calibration and privacy issues as B, multiplied by the number of phone models, and less convenient to manage.
